props.dek: A whole band rarely disappears. One musician out and a substitute in is the usual case. Here's how that works, what winter does to a mountain booking, and what to ask before you sign.

props.llms_description: What happens if a band or a musician cancels on a wedding or an event, from a Denver live-music booking company. A whole band rarely cancels; the usual case is one musician out and a substitute in, picked from players who already know the songs. The post lists what to ask about substitutes, explains how Colorado's Traction Law on I-70 between Dotsero and Morrison (September 1 through May 31) affects a mountain booking and why to ask whether the band drives up the day before, and says what a band's cancellation clause should cover. Signet's Backup Promise: if a musician or a whole act can't make the date, Signet replaces them with an act of the same style and size at no extra cost, and if the client would rather not have the replacement or none can be found, everything paid is returned.

items.text: A substitute musician is normal. What matters is who picks them and when you hear about it.
For a mountain event between September and May, ask where the band will be the night before.
Read what the contract says happens if the band cancels. It's a different clause from what happens if you do.

props.html:
Every planner who books live music has the same question somewhere in the back of their mind. What if the band doesn’t show up?

It’s a fair question. The answer depends less on luck than on a few things you can ask about before you sign.

A band is a handful of people with their own calendars, their own cars and their own colds. Most of what goes wrong is ordinary. Someone gets sick. A family emergency comes up. A van won’t start.

In Colorado you can add the road.

Working musicians keep a short list of players who already know their songs. When the bass player is out, the band calls the next bass player on that list. Most guests never notice.

The exception is the person out front. A substitute drummer is close to invisible. A substitute singer is a different act. So the questions worth asking are about who, and when:

  • Who picks the substitute, and do they already know the songs?
  • Will you tell me before the event, and will you tell me why?
  • If the singer or the bandleader is the one who can’t make it, is it still the act I booked?

props.text: What winter does to a mountain booking

props.html:
From September 1 through May 31, Colorado’s Traction Law is in effect on I-70 between Dotsero and Morrison. That’s the whole drive from Denver to Vail and Beaver Creek. Every car needs tires with at least 3/16 inch of tread rated for winter, all-weather or mud and snow, or chains or an approved traction device. In a bad storm, CDOT moves to the chain law, which it calls “the final safety measure before the highway is closed.”

A band hauling a trailer of gear up from Denver on the afternoon of a Vail wedding is counting on that road. So ask:

  • Is the band driving up the day of, or the day before?
  • If it’s the day of, what time do they leave, and what happens if I-70 closes?
  • Is there a band that lives up there? (For the Vail Valley, we have Quadrasonic.)

A night of lodging costs money, and it shows up on the quote. Here’s how to read the travel lines on a band quote. Our mountain planning page has the rest of what changes above the foothills.

props.text: What a band's cancellation policy should say

props.html:
A music contract has two cancellation clauses. One covers what happens if you cancel. The other covers what happens if the band cancels. The first one usually gets a paragraph. The second one sometimes gets a line.

Read the second one. Then ask:

  • If you cancel on me, do I get everything back?
  • Will you help me find a replacement, or am I on my own?
  • What counts as weather or “circumstances beyond our control,” and who decides the event is off?

Every booking with us comes with our Backup Promise. If a musician or a whole act can’t make your date, we replace them with an act of the same style and size at no extra cost. If you’d rather not have the replacement, or we can’t find one, you get back everything you’ve paid.
